note: All head-count values are project visual heuristics, not vendor-native parameters or medical/anatomical measurements. Hair buns, crowns, hairpins and other head ornaments are excluded from the visual head unit.

P7.label: natural
prompt_translation: Keep a natural adult human proportion with believable torso, pelvis, leg and foot relationships.

P8.label: elegant
prompt_translation: Make the figure elegantly tall and slender while preserving a complete believable torso and natural pelvis-to-knee-to-ankle segmentation.
Use a slightly smaller visual head-to-body relationship without changing the face identity or facial geometry.

P9.label: fashion
prompt_translation: Create a high-fashion nine-head visual proportion on a believable adult body: tall, elongated and elegant rather than anime-stretched.
Slightly reduce the head's visual share of the full figure while keeping face width, face shape and all identity geometry unchanged.
Keep the ribcage and torso fully developed; do not shorten the torso to create longer legs.
Lengthen the hip-to-knee and knee-to-ankle segments in balance, preserving natural knee position, pelvis width, ankle scale and foot proportion.
Raise the waistline only visually through sash placement, skirt-panel origin and vertical garment lines rather than compressing the anatomical torso.
Bias the costume toward vertical flow and slightly control sleeve/skirt lateral mass so the garment supports the tall fashion silhouette.

P9.5.label: stylized_fashion
prompt_translation: Use a deliberately stylized fashion-model proportion while keeping a complete believable torso and coordinated limb segmentation.
Do not create an extreme tiny waist, narrow pelvis, oversized feet, or isolated calf/thigh stretching.

rules: Hair buns, crowns, hairpins and head ornaments do not count toward the visual head unit.
Never create a smaller-looking head by narrowing the face, enlarging the shoulders, or changing facial identity.
Head-scale correction must be achieved through whole-figure relationship and framing, not facial reshaping.
Do not lengthen only the thigh or only the calf.
Keep knee placement believable relative to pelvis and ankle.
Preserve natural pelvis width and realistic lower-limb soft tissue.
Do not enlarge the feet after elongating the figure.
Use sash placement, skirt-panel origin and long vertical panel lines to support a taller silhouette without changing garment identity.
Reduce only excess lateral sleeve/skirt spread; do not redesign the costume or remove signature layers.
Preserve enough footwear visibility to clarify the full vertical figure.
